subject: Exec update: Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping (reliability program)
related_links: Linear: ENG-4830 (Remediation SLA mapping by category)
body:
From: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 6, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Exec update: Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping (reliability program)

Hi Ava,

Sharing a quick exec update on the reliability program workstream: “Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping.” The goal is to reduce paging ambiguity and handoff delays during live incidents, and to make trends/actioning measurable across Hosted + Dedicated (and Private where we’re primary operator).

What we’re doing (v1)
1) Standardize incident classification
- A small, on-call-friendly set of incident categories (top-level) + required metadata (impacted surface, region, tier, contributing factors).
- Designed to be usable during active response and stable enough for reporting.

2) Establish a single source of truth for ownership
- Map each category and major service surface to (a) a primary owning team/service, (b) escalation paths, and (c) expected “secondary” SMEs.
- Implemented in incident-bot so the owner is suggested/required early (reduce “who owns this?” time).

3) Define remediation SLAs (TTM/TTR)
- Targets by severity x category x customer tier.
- Includes expectations for customer comms (support + eng), and follow-up requirements (postmortem, action items).

Rollout plan (6–8 weeks)
- Discovery (1–2 wks): inventory last 2–3 quarters incidents; cluster top failure modes; draft candidate taxonomy.
- Design (2 wks): finalize taxonomy + metadata fields + ownership map; reviews with SRE/Platform/Runtime/Support.
- Tooling rollout (2–3 wks): incident-bot required fields, postmortem template update, dashboards.
- Backfill + baseline reporting (1 wk): normalize last 90 days; publish baseline and begin monthly review cadence.

Where we are now
- Draft taxonomy list + definitions are in review with SRE/Platform/Runtime.
- Ownership mapping is being validated against current on-call rotations (avoid “paper ownership”).
- Remediation SLA table is being aligned w/ Product + Support so it doesn’t conflict with contractual SLA language.

Expected impact (what we’ll measure)
- Reduce MTTR by decreasing time-to-owner + time-to-mitigate (current baseline from recent incident clustering: median MTTR ~45–60 min for the top recurring types; worst-case is driven by cross-team handoffs).
- Reduce incident recurrence in top categories by making “top offenders” visible and consistently attributed.
- Improve CS escalations by providing category-specific playbooks + clearer ETAs.

Exec asks / decisions needed
- Confirm that category + owner must be set at incident declaration (vs “within 15 minutes”). SRE recommendation is “at declare” with a small allowed “Unknown/Needs triage” escape hatch.
- Reinforce expectation that owning teams meet remediation SLAs (TTM/TTR targets) and that permanent fixes are tracked post-incident.

Attachments:
- Exec_Update_Incident_Taxonomy_Ownership_v1_2025-02-06.pdf
- Rollout_Checklist_IncidentBot_Postmortem_Dashboards_v1.xlsx

If helpful, Sean and Priya can do a 10-min readout in staff next week with the proposed taxonomy list and the ownership map for the top 10 categories.

Thanks,
Talia
Program Manager, SRE & Reliability
Redwood Inference


---

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 6, 2025 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Exec update: Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping (reliability program)

Thanks Talia — this is the right direction.

Two questions before we socialize broadly:
1) For Dedicated + enterprise accounts, how do the remediation SLAs here relate to contract SLA language and customer-facing comms? I don’t want us to accidentally promise something new/stronger in internal docs that CS will then repeat externally.

2) “Category + owner at declare” makes sense, but we need to make sure it doesn’t slow down declaration. What’s the fallback when we genuinely don’t know yet (e.g., widespread 5xx where it could be routing, gateway, or fleet)?

If you can clarify those, I’m good with a short staff readout next week.

Ava


---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 6, 2025 at 11:18 AM PT
Subject: Re: Exec update: Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping (reliability program)

On (1): We’re treating the remediation SLAs in this project as operational targets (TTM/TTR) to drive predictable response and reduce customer pain, but not as customer-promised contractual SLAs.

What will be customer-visible:
- For enterprise incidents, Support will use category-specific comms guidance (what we say, when we say it, and who approves), plus consistent ETAs language (“next update by X” vs “fixed by X”).
- Any statement that implies a contractual commitment stays anchored to existing contract SLA language. Marissa/Rachel are reviewing the table to ensure wording is aligned.

On (2): Agree we can’t slow declaration.
- The incident-bot flow will allow “Unknown / needs triage” for the first pass, but still require an owner (SRE/IC can set initial owner as “SRE/Incident Command” when unknown).
- Policy: category/owner must be updated within 15 minutes if initially unknown, and reclassified post-incident if needed.
- We’ll also implement owner auto-suggestion based on impacted surface selection (e.g., “Hosted API gateway/edge” vs “routing/control plane” vs “GPU fleet/capacity”) to reduce cognitive load.

Happy to do the 10-min staff readout with Priya (taxonomy + ownership map + rollout dates + success metrics).

Sean
SRE, Incident Command
Redwood Inference


---

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2025 at 8:05 AM PT
Subject: Re: Exec update: Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping (reliability program)

That works.

Let’s do the staff readout next week (10 min). Please include:
- the proposed v1 category list (top level only)
- the “Unknown/needs triage” rule + 15-min update expectation
- how we’ll keep the ownership map current (who approves changes)
- the initial baseline you’ll publish (MTTR/TTM by category/owner) and the monthly review cadence

Talia: please send me the proposed rollout date for incident-bot required fields once Devon confirms.

Ava
